narrative:
The model estimates a 71% chance that you will leave your current job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This prediction is driven primarily by three key aspects of your professional background.

Your total years of experience across all jobs stands out as the strongest factor pushing the prediction toward leaving. With 6-10 years overall, you fall into a group where many employees start exploring new opportunities rather than staying long-term. This has a stronger influence than most other details in your profile.

Next, the time you've spent in your current role—1 to 5 years—also pulls the prediction toward departure. While this duration is common among those expected to stay, the model sees it as signaling that you may be ready for a change after settling into the organization.

The third most influential element actually works in your favor: you have not received other job offers while at this company. This lack of external opportunities pushes the prediction slightly toward staying. However, it is not enough to outweigh the first two factors.

The organization should consider discussing your career goals with you directly and exploring ways to increase your sense of stability and recognition. You may want to reflect on whether your current path still aligns with your long-term plans. (218 words)
